Re: Appeal of denial for total ankle replacement, CPT 27702

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial dated August 25, 2026, for the requested total ankle replacement, CPT 27702. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

Please reconsider the request using the clinical documentation summarized below and the additional information submitted with this appeal.

The records establish moderate-to-severe, function-limiting ankle disease:

- I have had 14 months of progressive ankle pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- Weight-bearing radiographs dated June 18, 2026, show obliteration of the tibiotalar joint space with subchondral cysts.
- I have an antalgic gait and can walk only approximately two blocks.
- Provocative testing is positive on the affected side, and range of motion is limited by pain.
- I completed 24 supervised physical-therapy visits over 16 weeks, from March 13 through July 3, 2026, with treatment focused on ankle strengthening and balance.
- NSAID treatment for four months provided inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 19, 2026, provided only three weeks of partial relief.

The public BlueChoice medical-policy page identifies the policy as Total Ankle Replacement - CAM 70177. The policy states: “Total ankle replacement using an FDA approved device may be considered MEDICALLY NECESSARY in skeletally mature patients with moderate to severe ankle (tibiotalar) pain that limits daily activity and who have the following conditions:”

The policy then lists these qualifying conditions:

“Arthritis in adjacent joints (i.e., subtalar or midfoot); OR”

“Severe arthritis of the contralateral ankle; OR”

“Arthrodesis of the contralateral ankle; OR”

“Inflammatory (e.g., rheumatoid) arthritis”

The submitted records clearly address the policy’s pain and daily-activity requirements. They document severe structural tibiotalar disease, persistent pain despite conservative treatment, substantially restricted walking, an antalgic gait, and painful restricted motion.

The records also document the absence of several potential safety concerns. There is no active infection, BMI is 29, I am a nonsmoker, and there is no untreated substance use. Please also consider the surgeon’s clinical assessment and the complete imaging, examination, therapy, medication, and injection records.

To address any remaining documentation issue, please have the reviewing clinician identify specifically which policy element or medical record is missing rather than upholding the denial generally as incomplete. The current packet should be supplemented with the following information if required:

- [Affected ankle and confirmation of skeletal maturity]
- [Documentation of adjacent-joint arthritis, severe contralateral-ankle arthritis, contralateral-ankle arthrodesis, or inflammatory arthritis, as applicable]
- [Documentation addressing any contraindications or relative contraindications not already covered]
- [Confirmation of the FDA-approved device to be used]
- [Surgeon training and experience with the proposed ankle-arthroplasty device and technique]
- [Proposed surgery date and facility]

The policy also states: “Total ankle replacement is considered INVESTIGATIONAL for all other indications.” This appeal therefore requests that the plan identify which qualifying indication it believes has not been documented and allow the treating surgeon to provide that information before making a final determination.

The policy further states: “Patients should have no functional barriers to participation in a rehabilitation program.” I have completed an extensive supervised rehabilitation program consisting of 24 visits over 16 weeks, which supports my ability to participate in postoperative rehabilitation.

Please overturn the denial and approve the requested total ankle replacement. If the plan maintains the denial, please provide the specific medical-policy criterion that was not met, the records that were considered incomplete, and the clinical rationale for the decision.

This appeal must be received by February 21, 2027, within 180 days of the denial notice. Please send the appeal determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Riley Lawson
